line: One device batch of up to 8,192 tokens runs at a time.  Text requests that wait for the device share a batch, oldest first, and a lone request runs at once.  A request with images or audio runs in a batch of its own, in arrival order, and its soft tokens count toward the batch.  A request that fits in one batch never spans two.  A larger request is split, and after each of its batches the requests that arrived meanwhile go first, so a short request waits for at most one batch of a long one.  A device failure that a probe confirms answers 503 `device_lost` and shuts the server down for its supervisor to restart, as the text server does.  Attention is bidirectional, so there is no cache to reuse between requests.  Gufo checks for cancellation before each batch that would take a request's inputs, so a cancelled request does not use the device again.  `--served-model-name` sets the public model ID.  Gufo supports only BF16 safetensors, not GGUF or quantized variants.
